questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it is a good university but also good social life among students

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think that there were a lot of things missing of my exhange. Everything were really closes down due to Corona therefore I think the start was difficult. Also the information before going were poor - late information and no information e.g. regarding housing.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think there were a lot of information missing e.g. regarding choosing courses. It came really late.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was the Erasmus Coordinator who was really helpfull when I had any question! He was really great

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The office gave some suggestion for places and webpages when I asked. However, I was really disappointed about how that handled housing. We were only two master students on economics thus I think it would have been natural to have put us together in a student house.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Do it in good time. A lot of people are not willing to rent to exchange student since we are only there for a short period of time

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: When got the information it was easy to register

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They use Mobility online for applying and formal stuff. Otherwise an internal portal called Portal2 for course registration. For the seminars you are to send a mail to the coordinator

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The coordinator and student office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: This was okay

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Maybe be more patient then me and read all the emails carefully

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think it was ok

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In the exercises the prof. are answering the exercise sheet for you. There is no teamwork or time to work on-campus on this.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. remember you can "shop" between courses in the beginning to see what you like 
2. Don't take too many seminars 
3. Take some good trips with the train - really easy
